text:
Ethan Park: trying to close on where mirroring lives for Shadow Traffic. options we keep circling: (1) gateway fan-out (2) runtime hook/sidecar (3) queue-based replay from telemetry. need a decision for ENG-2420 schema work so we can validate/enforce sampling safely.

Benji Okafor: +1. if policy schema is the source of truth (RoutePolicy), we need to know which component is the policy enforcement point.

Jordan Lee: my take: gateway fan-out is simplest to guarantee “doesn’t touch primary response” bc we can async fire-and-forget shadow request after primary request is accepted.

Vikram Singh: gateway fan-out looks simple on paper but can be messy:
- need to duplicate auth headers / customer context
- openai-compat layer does extra transforms; mirrored payload has to match the final runtime request, not the raw incoming
- risk of extra CPU at gateway for serialization, esp w/ streaming

Emily Zhao: runtime hook has the cleanest access to the canonical request object (post-normalization). but we need to be very very sure we don’t add latency / block on any shadow path.

Amara Diallo: gateway can enforce sampling + rate limits at the edge though. runtime hook means sampling happens deeper in stack unless we plumb the decision down.

Cole Summers: on enforcement: we can do “two-stage”:
1) policy engine decides shadow eligibility (route/customer/region + sample rate)
2) data plane enforces budgets (token-based cost guardrail) + drops if over
so even if stage 1 misconfigured, stage 2 keeps fleet safe.

Mina Haddad: for routing, runtime already has model selection / fallback logic. mirroring in runtime lets us mirror AFTER we pick the primary target, which is useful for analysis (“compare to shadow target vs the actual primary target chosen”). gateway fan-out won’t know about the final route decision unless we return it.

Ravi Menon: also policy evaluation should be deterministic + consistent across retries. gateway sees client retries; runtime sees internal retries. which matters for sampling? if you sample at gateway you can double-sample due to retries.

Jordan Lee: we can key sampling on request_id and persist the decision in headers from gateway -> runtime.

Benji Okafor: that implies request_id must be generated at gateway always, even for non-shadow flows. is that already true?

Ethan Park: request_id exists but not guaranteed to be set at the “front door” in all ingress paths (some internal calls). we can standardize but it’s a change.

Thomas Baird: re: safe sampling, please don’t use raw user_id / prompt content to hash. cardinality + privacy. ideally use `request_id` only.

Sean Gallagher: SRE lens: whichever path we choose needs:
- kill switch that does not require deploy
- hard cap on shadow QPS and GPU budget
- and failures MUST be isolated (no cascading backpressure into primary)
gateway fan-out still consumes downstream capacity if shadow target is in same cluster.

Emily Zhao: runtime hook doesn’t have to mean “in-band”. we can push a minimal “shadow job” to a queue from runtime and return immediately.

Vikram Singh: yeah, think: runtime emits to local async worker (or external queue) with strict timeout (like 2ms) for enqueue. if enqueue fails, drop shadow and increment a counter.

Amara Diallo: if runtime is doing enqueue, gateway loses ability to protect itself from bursty customers turning sampling to 100% by accident.

Cole Summers: budgets should live close to the expensive resource anyway (GPU pool / shadow runner). gateway rate limits help but won’t capture actual cost. we should budget on estimated tokens * sample rate.

Jordan Lee: what about putting mirroring in gateway but shadow runner is in separate queue + pool. gateway enqueues shadow job, not send full request to model.

Vikram Singh: still has the “payload canonicalization” issue. gateway would have to either:
- enqueue raw request and replay later (dangerous; replay semantics change)
- or implement the same normalization as runtime (dup logic)

Mina Haddad: +1 to avoiding duplicate normalization. we’ll get subtle diffs on tool-calls, streaming, etc.

Benji Okafor: if runtime is the canonical place, ENG-2420 schema should assume the runtime can read `shadow_traffic` config on the resolved route. policy engine should output something like “shadow_decision: yes/no + targets + sample_key”.

Ethan Park: this is the crux: do we let data plane decide sample? or does control plane precompute? my preference: policy engine computes “should_shadow” given route/customer/region, but sampling decision (the random draw) happens in data plane using request_id hash. that avoids needing per-request calls to policy.

Thomas Baird: please include “bucketed sampling” spec in ENG-2420. i.e. `hash(request_id) % 10000 < sample_rate_bps` so it’s stable and easy to reason about.

Emily Zhao: also we need “shadow disabled by default” + “max sample rate cap” server-side. config should be rejected if > cap unless admin override.

Amara Diallo: cap where? gateway? control plane validation? runtime? ideally all 3. but at least control plane validation so misconfig never ships.

Cole Summers: +1. defense in depth:
- control plane validation: enforce `0 <= sample_rate_bps <= 500` (example) for beta
- runtime: enforce local cap too (in case stale config)
- shadow runner: enforce budget limiter + queue backpressure

Jordan Lee: concerns w/ runtime hook: any extra work in the hot path. even computing hashes for every request adds something.

Vikram Singh: hashing request_id is trivial. we already do tracing IDs etc. bigger overhead is if we accidentally serialize full prompts. rule should be: only enqueue redacted/approved fields and never block.

Sean Gallagher: can we formalize “no waits” as:
- enqueue attempt max 1-2ms
- no retries in-band
- shadow is best-effort, drop on pressure
and we alert on drop rate / queue depth.

Mina Haddad: also shadow needs to respect per-customer allowlists. some enterprise will opt out. that check is policy-level, not data plane.

Benji Okafor: ok so proposal emerging:
1) policy schema (ENG-2420) adds `shadow_traffic` block on RoutePolicy
2) control plane validates sample caps + allowlist format
3) runtime evaluates allowlist/region gating using request context + computes sampling decision from request_id
4) runtime enqueues shadow job to shadow-runner queue (async) w/ strict timeout
5) shadow runner executes on separate capacity + budgets

Ethan Park: yep. that’s basically “runtime-triggered queue-based shadow” vs gateway fan-out.

Jordan Lee: i’m ok with this if we explicitly say gateway should NOT attempt to mirror full request to avoid divergence.

Emily Zhao: +1. and we should add a header / trace attr for `shadow_sampled=true/false` for debugging.

Thomas Baird: and a tag allowlist. if we’re adding `shadow_target_id`, it must be bounded (config-defined) not arbitrary strings.

Ravi Menon: one more: sampling should happen after auth + route resolution, but before model execution. that way we can include primary model/version info in the shadow job metadata.

Ethan Park: action items:
- Benji: update ENG-2420 draft schema w/ `shadow_traffic` fields (sample_rate_bps, targets[], customer_allowlist?, region_allowlist?, enabled)
- Emily/Vikram: confirm runtime hook point post-normalization
- Cole/Sean: propose beta caps + budget defaults
we’ll document “why not gateway fan-out” in ADR draft.

Benji Okafor: ack. will post a schema snippet in ENG-2420 later today.

Sean Gallagher: please include kill switch semantics in schema too (global + per-route), even if wiring is later. easier for ops.

Ethan Park: noted. we can add `disabled_reason`? or at least ensure there’s a global override path.

Jordan Lee: reaction from me: :thumbsup: as long as we don’t regress gateway p99.

Mina Haddad: :+1: runtime-triggered means smarter routing metadata for analysis.

Thomas Baird: :eyes: on any metric dimensions you add. loop me in before we ship tags.

Cole Summers: +1. budget limiter design doc coming.

Ethan Park: closing loop: decision = implement mirroring trigger in runtime (post-normalization) and enqueue to shadow runner queue. gateway fan-out rejected due to normalization divergence + retry double-sampling risk. will reference this thread in ENG-2420 + ADR.
